skill.name: playwright-browser
skill.description: Control Playwright browser sessions from a CLI to navigate pages, inspect accessibility trees, interact with elements, and capture screenshots.
skill.summary: Automate browser navigation and accessible page interactions through documented Playwright CLI commands.
skill.author: Bind

security_audit.summary: All 41 command findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks and documented Bun commands. The two hardcoded URLs are benign navigation examples that are not contacted automatically. Persistent cookies and localStorage create a medium risk when the browser profile contains authenticated session data.

remediation.issue: Browser profiles persist cookies and localStorage in the project directory.
remediation.suggestion: Document profile cleanup, restrict filesystem permissions, exclude .playwright-data from version control, and require confirmation before reusing authenticated sessions.

static_findings.snippet: - `ref` - Element reference (role:name, text:content, or CSS selector)
- `--press <key>` - Press a key after typing (e.g., Enter, Tab)
- `ref` - Element reference (role:name, text:content, or CSS selector)
Commands that interact with elements (`type`, `click`) accept flexible element references:
1. Use `snapshot` to see the accessibility tree
- Browser data is stored in `.playwright-data/` in the project root

semantic_findings.title: Persistent Browser Session Data
semantic_findings.description: The documented browser profile retains cookies and localStorage in .playwright-data. Authenticated session data may remain on disk and be reused by later commands.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: SKILL.md explicitly states the storage path and persistence of cookies and localStorage. These records commonly contain sensitive session state.

content.value_statement: Manual browser checks are slow and difficult to repeat. This skill guides Playwright CLI sessions for navigation, accessible interaction, and screenshots.
actual_capabilities: Starts, checks, and stops persistent Playwright browser sessions.
Navigates the active browser session to a supplied URL.
Returns an accessibility tree for page inspection.
Types text, presses a key, and clicks referenced elements.
Captures viewport or full-page screenshots to a selected path.
limitations: The audited package contains instructions and metadata, but no executable browser scripts.
Bun, Playwright, and the referenced local scripts must already be available.
Website authentication, network restrictions, and anti-automation controls can prevent completion.
Persistent browser data can retain sensitive cookies and localStorage between sessions.

use_cases.title: Repeat Interface Checks
use_cases.description: Navigate test pages, inspect accessible elements, perform routine interactions, and capture visual evidence.

use_cases.title: Inspect Accessible Structure
use_cases.description: Read the accessibility tree and identify stable role-based references before testing an interface.

use_cases.title: Collect Page Screenshots
use_cases.description: Open selected pages and capture viewport or full-page screenshots for documentation and review.

prompt_templates.title: Open and Inspect a Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Open [URL], take an accessibility snapshot, and summarize the main interactive elements.

prompt_templates.title: Capture a Full Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Start a headless session, open [URL], wait for loading, and capture a full-page screenshot named [filename].

prompt_templates.title: Complete a Search Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Open [URL], inspect the page, enter [query] in the search field, submit it, and summarize the visible results.

prompt_templates.title: Validate an Application Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Test [workflow] on [URL] with role-based references, capture each checkpoint, report failures, and stop before irreversible actions.

output_examples.input: Open the documentation site and identify the primary navigation controls.
output_examples.output: Opened the page and found navigation links for Guides, API Reference, Examples, and Support.

output_examples.input: Search the product catalog for wireless keyboards and summarize the visible results.
output_examples.output: Submitted the search and found twelve visible results. The first items include compact, ergonomic, and mechanical keyboard models.

output_examples.input: Capture a full-page screenshot of the release notes.
output_examples.output: Captured the loaded release notes page and saved the full-page image to the requested filename.

best_practices: Take an accessibility snapshot before interactions and prefer role-based references.
Review target domains and requested actions before sending data or changing account state.
Stop sessions after use and protect or remove .playwright-data when it contains sensitive state.
anti_patterns: Do not enter passwords, tokens, or personal data into untrusted pages.
Do not use fragile CSS selectors when accessible roles and names are available.
Do not leave persistent sessions running or browser profiles exposed in shared projects.

faq.question: Does this skill install Playwright?
faq.answer: No installation workflow is documented. Bun, Playwright, and the referenced scripts must already be available.

faq.question: Can the browser run without a visible window?
faq.answer: Yes. Start the session with the documented headless option.

faq.question: How does the skill find page elements?
faq.answer: It supports accessibility role and name references, text references, and CSS selectors.

faq.question: Can it work with signed-in websites?
faq.answer: Persistent cookies and localStorage can retain sign-in state. Protect the browser profile and confirm sensitive actions.

faq.question: What screenshot options are documented?
faq.answer: It can save to a selected path and capture either the viewport or the full page.

faq.question: What should I do when an element is not found?
faq.answer: Take a new accessibility snapshot, verify the element reference, and retry with its current role and name.
